_about: Narrator card: who this voice is, and the few habits he keeps from one video to the next. Everything else (how a video opens, how steps start, which fillers go where, the slips, the endings, the phrases) changes from video to video: scripts/script/style.py draws it, scripts/script/variety.py checks it. These habits are the exception: the history check allows them to repeat across videos, at about the rate given, and never more than max_per_video in one video. One recognisable person on different days, not a different person each video.
name: Alex
who: Has used the product for a while and is showing a friend how he does it. Relaxed, plain, a bit dry. Never salesy, never excited about a button. Says what he'd actually do, and skips what he wouldn't bother with.

habits.what: His filler is "uh". "Um" turns up too, but less, and only where a real pause follows.
His hedge: "that's pretty much it for the form", "it's pretty much the same page".

Said under his breath when something he did shows up, always inside a sentence with words before and after it: "I hit save and there we go, it's on the list". Never its own line, never the start or end of a sentence ("There we go." as a cheerful line of its own is banned; the checker refuses it). Rare: casual demos say it about once in nine minutes.

How he hunts, when he really has to look (rare: only where explore flagged it as hard to find, in SaaS demos): "where've they put it" or "hang on". The words can repeat across videos; the hunt itself stays rare.

_changed: 12 Nov 2026: "which is handy" removed (heard as a stock aside in both rewrites back to back); "there we go" down to 1 video in 10 and inside a sentence only. Habits come out by their rate only; none is forced to keep him recognisable.
